title: Auto Loans: Payment Extension Allowances
content:
Auto Loans borrowers can have installments pushed back to the close of the loan through a payment extension. The allowances below fix, per product, what an extension costs, how many installments one extension can move, how often extensions may be granted, and how seasoned the loan must be.

## Allowance table

| Loan product | Fee per extension granted (USD) | Most installments moved by one extension | Most extensions in any rolling 365 days | Most extensions over the life of the loan | Whole months since funding required | Installments already paid required |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Used Vehicle Loan | 35.00 | 2 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 6 |
| Certified Pre-Owned Vehicle Loan | 35.00 | 2 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 6 |
| Auto Refinance Loan | 35.00 | 2 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 6 |
| Lease Buyout Loan | 35.00 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 6 | 6 |
| New Vehicle Loan | 35.00 | 2 | 2 | 6 | 6 | 6 |
| Green Vehicle Loan | 35.00 | 2 | 2 | 6 | 6 | 6 |

## Column notes

- The fee is charged once for each extension that is granted, whatever the number of installments it moves.
- "Most installments moved" is a per-extension ceiling: a single extension may move one installment or up to that many.
- The rolling count looks back over any 365-day span, not over a calendar year.
- The lifetime ceiling covers the whole life of the loan from funding, and it is the only allowance that differs by product: three on the Lease Buyout Loan, six on the New and Green Vehicle Loans, four elsewhere.
- Loan seasoning is measured two ways, in whole months since funding and in scheduled installments already paid; both columns read six on every product.
